claims.claim: Best Start Grant has three payments.
claims.quote: The 3 Best Start Grant payments are:
claims.note: The source identifies three grant payments.

claims.claim: Each grant payment is one-off for a child.
claims.quote: If responsibility for the child changes, they may make extra payments to the person who’s now responsible for the child.
claims.note: The source says payments are usually made once per child, but permits extra payments when responsibility for the child changes.

claims.claim: Best Start Grant is for eligible families in Scotland.
claims.quote: If you live in England, Wales or Northern Ireland, you cannot get Best Start Grant or Best Start Foods.
claims.note: The source confines this grant to Scotland.

claims.claim: Pregnancy and Baby Payment is £796.65 for the first child.
claims.quote: £796.65 for your first child.
claims.note: The base first-child rate is stated.

claims.claim: Pregnancy and Baby Payment is £398.35 for other children.
claims.quote: You may get the £796.65 payment if:
claims.note: The usual subsequent-child rate is £398.35, but listed exceptions award £796.65 to some later children.

claims.claim: Early Learning Payment is £331.95.
claims.quote: £331.95 to help with the costs of early learning.
claims.note: The payment amount is stated.

claims.claim: School Age Payment is £331.95.
claims.quote: School Age Payment is a payment of £331.95 per child.
claims.note: The payment amount is stated.

claims.claim: Normally the applicant or partner needs Universal Credit, Pension Credit, income-related ESA, income-based JSA, Income Support or Housing Benefit.
claims.quote: To get Best Start Grant and Foods, normally you or your partner need to get one of these: Universal Credit Housing Benefit Income Support Pension Credit income-based Jobseekers Allowance (JSA) income-related Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
claims.note: The page names all six benefits and the normal applicant-or-partner condition.

claims.claim: You can apply while a decision on a qualifying benefit is pending.
claims.quote: If you're not getting any of these benefits or payments, but have applied for one, you can still apply for Best Start Grant and Best Start Foods.
claims.note: The page permits applying after a qualifying benefit application.

claims.claim: Applicants under 18 need no qualifying benefit.
claims.quote: If you're under 18, you do not need to be on any payments or benefits to get Best Start Grant or Best Start Foods.
claims.note: The source expressly exempts under-18 applicants from the benefit condition.

claims.claim: Some 18- or 19-year-olds without their own qualifying benefit can qualify through a parent or carer.
claims.quote: If you're 18 or 19 and do not get any benefits or payments, you can still apply for Best Start Grant or Best Start Foods. Your parent or carer needs to get one of these for you: Child Benefit Universal Credit child payments the child addition part of Pension Credit
claims.note: The parent or carer must receive a specified benefit payment for the young applicant.
